name: Ballet routine

card.summary: Ballet-style training, barre and stretching work used to build posture, balance, flexibility and a long, graceful physique.
card.note: Intensive training is associated with overuse injuries; elite settings link to low energy availability.

quick.overview:
A ballet routine borrows classical ballet training, with its barre exercises, posture work, turnout, stretching and balance drills, to improve how someone carries and shapes their body.

People use it for upright posture, flexibility, coordination and a lean, elongated look. Systematic reviews of ballet interventions report improvements in balance, particularly in novices, while strength results are mixed.
quick.how: Practitioners take adult beginner or recreational classes, or follow barre-style home sessions, and combine them with other exercise. Classes typically move through barre, centre work and stretching.
quick.risks: Reviews link ballet training to overuse injuries, especially when technique is forced, and to lower arm bone density in teen dancers. Pointe work is typically introduced only after sufficient strength and training.

lead: A ballet routine, in looksmaxxing usage, is ballet-style training adopted to improve posture, poise and physique. Classical ballet requires balance, strength and range of motion, and recreational classes are open to adults and beginners.[4]

Ballet itself grew out of Italian Renaissance courts and was developed in France and Russia; several teaching methods, including the French, Vaganova, Cecchetti, Bournonville, Royal Academy of Dance and Balanchine methods, shape how it is taught.[9] People who add it to their routines cite upright carriage, flexibility and a long-lined look.

Research on ballet training covers balance, bone density, injuries and fitness. A systematic review of 23 intervention studies found balance improved in most studies of novice dancers, while strength gains in experienced dancers were reported in only a quarter.[4] A forum thread on looksmax.org titled 'Ballet routine' exists but is a short joke post.[10]

chain: Better balance, flexibility and body control
More upright posture and a lean, elongated look
angle.text: Practitioners use ballet-style training for posture and graceful movement. Research supports balance gains in novices, and flexibility and carriage are the commonly described appearance benefits.

paras: Ballet classes follow a structure of barre exercises, centre work and jumps, with early instruction centred on standing posture and alignment.[9] Training is a long process of physical preparation that often begins in childhood.[5]

Ballet class does not provide a large aerobic stimulus, and dancers often show low aerobic fitness; the review also notes dancers' reluctance to add training they believe causes undesirable muscle growth.[5] Jumping demands in professional class have been measured in elite dancers.[8]

A 2020 systematic review of 23 intervention studies (at least 4 weeks) found that balance improved in 75% of studies of novices that measured it, while only 25% of studies in experienced dancers reported strength improvements.[4] A review of equilibrium studies compared dancers with non-dancers and across experience levels.[6] A randomized trial in 45 female dancers compared static and PNF stretching for hip adductor flexibility.[7] A 2024 study examined classical ballet for women over 50 for balance, strength and range of motion.[11]

A meta-analysis of pre-professional adolescent female dancers found lower bone density at the radius and higher at the femoral neck, with no difference at the lumbar spine or tibia, based on low-quality cross-sectional studies.[3]

A paediatric review identified overuse injuries as the most common ballet injuries, with forced turnout the most common technique error.[2] Readiness for pointe is assessed on maturity, strength and flexibility, usually around ages 11 to 13.[1] Ballet dancers have shown higher risk of several eating disorders in a 2014 meta-analysis described on Wikipedia, and eating and weight-control behaviours of young dancers have been studied.[9][12]

timeline.event: Louis XIV founds the Académie Royale de Danse.[9]
La Sylphide, considered the first Romantic ballet.[9]
Balanchine's Apollo, regarded as the first neoclassical ballet.[9]

lore.intro: Ballet appears in looksmaxxing talk mostly in passing, as a posture or grace practice; the only dedicated thread found is a joke post.[10]

claims.claim: Ballet-style training improves posture and grace
claims.believers: Adopters describe upright carriage and body control as the payoff.[10]
claims.experts: Systematic reviews report balance gains in novices; posture outcomes specifically have not been established.[4]
